target.name: Unlimited Industries
target.founder: Alex Modon, Jordan Stern, Tara Viswanathan

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $12M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Unlimited Industries is a seed-stage housing and construction company founded by Alex Modon, Jordan Stern, and Tara Viswanathan. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of five private construction-tech companies: BotBuilt, Apis Cor, Ground Control Development, ADMARES, and Hedral. No directly comparable public companies trade in this subsector, limiting benchmarking options.

The stage-progression method provides the primary valuation signal. Using the company's $12M in total capital raised as a proxy for seed-stage value and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $30M. This methodology assumes the $12M raised approximates pre-money or early post-money value and that similar-stage construction-tech companies experience comparable step-up multiples upon advancing rounds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, with $30M as the median point. Key uncertainties include: the actual post-money valuation embedded in the $12M raise; burn rate and runway relative to next funding milestones; and whether private-market comparables in this emerging subsector exhibit the assumed 2.5x progression. The single-method triangulation also reflects data constraints—additional approaches such as revenue or EBITDA multiples would require operational metrics not provided here. This range should be stress-tested against company-specific execution risk and macro construction-sector conditions.
